description: Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, security risks, prompt injection, data exfiltration, and supply-chain risks in Claude Code, Codex, and MCP skills before you install them.

written.description: Checks an agent skill before you install it, following the files it pulls in and asking a model whether any of it is trying to misdirect the agent. Each verdict carries the provenance behind it.

alive.last_commit_message:
fix(e5): distinguish proved cloud downloads from uploads (#891)

* test: cover cloud download direction and upload controls

Signed-off-by: Christopher Kevin <christopherk@nvidia.com>

* fix(e5): distinguish literal cloud downloads from uploads

Signed-off-by: Christopher Kevin <christopherk@nvidia.com>

* refactor(e5): bound download indexing and simplify option parsing

Signed-off-by: Christopher Kevin <christopherk@nvidia.com>

* fix(e5): retain findings after shell lookup and directory changes

Signed-off-by: Christopher Kevin <christopherk@nvidia.com>

* fix(e5): retain findings after unproved shell setup

Signed-off-by: Christopher Kevin <christopherk@nvidia.com>

* fix(e5): end preamble comments only at newlines

The download proof split the preamble with str.splitlines(), which also
breaks at form feeds, vertical tabs, lone carriage returns and Unicode
separators. Shells end a line, and so a comment, only at a newline, so
"\f# ; aws() { custom "$@"; }" still defines aws() while the proof skipped
it as a comment and dropped E5 for the rebound transfer.

Reject the proof when the preamble contains any logical line break other
than LF or CRLF, the same rule _sc2_logical_command applies to the command
itself, and split the preamble on LF only. Add regressions for every such
break before a rebinding, and CRLF variants of the supported preambles.

Signed-off-by: Narendran Raghavan <nraghavan@nvidia.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e5): accept only plain shell shebangs in the download proof

The preamble scan treated every leading "#" line as a comment, including
the shebang. When a script is executed directly, a shebang such as
"#!/usr/bin/env -S PATH=./bin:/usr/bin:/bin bash" or one setting BASH_ENV
or ZDOTDIR runs setup that rebinds aws or gsutil before the transfer, yet
the proof still dropped E5.

Keep the exemption only for a first-line shebang naming sh, bash, dash,
ksh or zsh under /bin, /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin, directly or through env,
with at most -e/-u options. Any other shebang keeps the finding. Add
regressions for env -S assignments, interpreter options, relative and
non-shell interpreters, and supported-shebang variants.

Signed-off-by: Narendran Raghavan <nraghavan@nvidia.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
